Retrieving and downloading data

Source: vignettes/retrieval.Rmd
retrieval.Rmd

Retrieve a dataset by ID or search result with tbod_get_dataset(). For a public ArcGIS layer URL, use tbod_get_arcgis_layer(). These examples need internet access and do not run during site builds.

Retrieve and filter records 

library(tampaBayOpenData)

permits <- tbod_get_dataset(
  "construction-permits",
  where = "PROJECTSTATUS IS NOT NULL",
  fields = c("RECORD_ID", "PROJECTSTATUS", "LASTUPDATE"),
  limit = 100
)
head(permits)
tbod_provenance(permits)[c("matched_rows", "returned_rows", "complete", "integrity")]

This returns up to 100 active permit-viewer rows. LASTUPDATE is an update time, not an issue date.

Provenance gives matching and returned counts. complete is TRUE only when all matches were returned.

where uses ArcGIS SQL; fields needs exact source names. Inspect them with tbod_dataset_info("construction-permits", refresh = TRUE)$fields. See ?tbod_get_dataset for advanced query filters.

Omit limit to retrieve all matches. Use order_by for a repeatable order when supported. Shortcuts include tbod_get_permits(), tbod_get_development_cases(), and tbod_get_capital_projects().

Retrieve a discovery row:

found <- tbod_search_datasets("housing", source = "live", portals = "city")
if (nrow(found)) {
  housing <- tbod_get_dataset(found[1, ], limit = 100)
  tbod_provenance(housing)[c("publisher", "item_id", "validation_status")]
}

Or use a layer URL ending in /FeatureServer/<id> or /MapServer/<id>:

yard_waste <- tbod_get_arcgis_layer(
  "https://arcgis.tampagov.net/arcgis/rest/services/OpenData/SolidWaste/MapServer/4",
  limit = 10
)
tbod_provenance(yard_waste)$validation_status # "not_checked"

Direct URLs have not_checked status. Review their source and reuse terms.

Check the live schema

tbod_schema() reads the saved schema; refresh = TRUE reads the service. Compare them with tbod_check_schema():

expected <- tbod_schema("construction-permits")
report <- tbod_check_schema("construction-permits")
report$status
report$issues[, c("category", "severity", "field", "expected", "actual")]

The report lists affected fields, expected and actual definitions, and severity.

Compatible additions warn. Missing fields, type changes, and incompatible geometry, CRS, object-ID, or endpoint changes stop retrieval.

For a direct or newly discovered layer, save a baseline yourself:

# Replace this example address with a public ArcGIS layer URL.
url <- "https://example.org/arcgis/rest/services/Example/FeatureServer/0"
baseline <- tbod_schema(url, refresh = TRUE)
later <- tbod_check_schema(url, expected = baseline)

Retrieval checks and timeouts

Retrieval checks counts and object IDs. Missing, repeated, or unexpected records stop the request. Large bounded previews may check a subset manifest; full manifests are limited to one million matches. Use a narrower where filter for larger sources. See ?tbod_get_dataset for integrity options.

These checks cannot freeze attributes while a live service is being updated.

timeout limits each HTTP attempt. total_timeout defaults to 120 seconds for retrieval, 90 for discovery, and 60 for metadata. Use Inf to remove the overall deadline. Parsing may finish after the deadline before an error is reported.

Attempts default to 30 seconds, with a 10-second connection limit. Adjust connection timing or add a delay between requests:

options(tampaBayOpenData.connect_timeout = 15,
        tampaBayOpenData.request_delay = 0.2)
# Restore defaults:
options(tampaBayOpenData.connect_timeout = NULL,
        tampaBayOpenData.request_delay = NULL)

Delays apply to every attempt, including retries, and count toward the overall timeout. Separate R processes are not coordinated.

Temporary failures and rate limits are retried; permanent errors stop immediately. Set the retry limit for this session:

options(tampaBayOpenData.max_retries = 2L)
# Restore the default later with:
options(tampaBayOpenData.max_retries = NULL)

Retries use increasing delays. Retry-After takes precedence up to 30 seconds; a longer server-requested wait stops the operation.

To identify your application, set options(tampaBayOpenData.user_agent = "my-project/1.0 (contact: me@example.org)"). Set it to NULL to restore the default.

Types and spatial results

Source column names and text are preserved. ArcGIS date-times usually become UTC POSIXct; unknown-zone values remain milliseconds with a warning. Date-only fields become Date. Other date/time types retain source strings.

Install sf and request spatial = TRUE for geometry. Use out_sr = 4326 for WGS 84, or omit it to keep the native CRS.

projects <- tbod_get_dataset(
  "development-cases", spatial = TRUE, out_sr = 4326
)
boundary <- tbod_get_dataset(
  "city-boundary", fields = "OBJECTID", spatial = TRUE, out_sr = 4326
)
sf::st_crs(projects)$epsg

Both results are sf tables. The CRS check should print 4326.

Exclude empty case geometries before plotting:

mapped_projects <- projects[!sf::st_is_empty(projects), ]

plot(
  sf::st_geometry(boundary),
  col = "#EDF4F6", border = "#7898A5", lwd = 1.2,
  axes = TRUE, graticule = TRUE, col_graticule = "#DCE7EB",
  xlab = "Longitude", ylab = "Latitude",
  main = "Active development cases in Tampa"
)
if (nrow(mapped_projects) > 0L) {
  case_fill <- grDevices::adjustcolor("#E76F51", alpha.f = 0.7)
  plot(sf::st_geometry(mapped_projects), add = TRUE, pch = 21,
       bg = case_fill, col = "#9B4934", cex = 0.85)
  graphics::legend(
    "bottomleft", legend = "Development case location", pch = 21,
    pt.bg = case_fill, col = "#9B4934", bg = "white",
    box.col = "#DCE7EB", cex = 0.85
  )
}

Dots are active case features. They may overlap, and rows without geometry remain in the data but are absent from the map.

The shoreline-adjusted city outline is map context, not a legal survey. See coverage for source limits.

Resume a large download

tbod_download_dataset() saves RDS chunks without collecting all pages in memory. Its ID manifest still has the one-million-match limit. Use tbod_download_arcgis_layer() for direct URLs.

saved <- tbod_download_dataset(
  "construction-permits",
  path = "~/tampaBayOpenData-downloads/permits",
  fields = c("OBJECTID", "RECORD_ID", "LASTUPDATE"),
  page_size = 500,
  total_timeout = 600
)
saved$complete
first_chunk <- readRDS(saved$files[[1]])
tbod_provenance(first_chunk)

saved$files lists chunk paths. Check that files exist before reading one when your filter may match no records.

Repeat the same call to resume. Saved chunks, settings, schema, and IDs are rechecked. Changed settings or membership require a new empty directory. saved$complete describes the whole download; individual chunks do not. Live records may change between sessions.

Downloads default to no overall deadline. Interrupted chunks can be resumed. If R was terminated, confirm it has stopped before removing a leftover empty .lock directory.

Troubleshooting common errors

  • Unknown ID: Search the catalog and use an ID from the results.
  • Timeout or rate limit: Try later, or increase the time budget.
  • Schema change: Inspect current fields and run tbod_check_schema().
  • Missing or repeated records: Retry or narrow where.
  • Cannot resume: Keep existing files and use a new empty directory.

See coverage for attribution and discovery for search limits.
